title: 5 Key Statistics About the State of Incentive Programs
summary: Disruption has become the norm as incentive planners brace for continued uncertainty in 2027.

title: Some Event Line Items Have Increased By 146% Since 2019
summary: Inflation is slowing, but event pricing isn’t turning around, according to a new price index from Maritz. Planners who keep cutting last year’s program to fit this year’s budget will lose on both cost and experience.

title: What If AI Thinks Your Event Is Canceled?
summary: New research from Freeman shows that one in five attendees now uses AI to find conferences. Will it be able to find the right information about yours?

summary: Hotels still treat trafficking awareness as a reputational risk rather than a duty of care. Planners who control room blocks are the buyers with the power to change that — but few are doing so.

title: Why Late Event Registration Doesn’t Actually Exist Anymore
summary: Event organizers keep asking why attendees are registering late. The real problem may be that they’re asking people to commit before giving them enough information, flexibility, or value to say yes.

title: Even Las Vegas Needs a Rain Plan: Record Storm Snarls IMEX Arrivals
summary: By the time IMEX’s show floor opens Tuesday, Sunday's record rain will be forgotten. The lesson shouldn’t be: A destination’s weather history is no longer a forecast.

title: FICP’s New President on Intentional Connection and Growth
summary: Just a couple of weeks into the job, Jamie Murdock already has a strong grasp of what makes this association different from others and how to introduce change.

summary: Your strongest promoters are not the ones working from inside your company — they're the people already coming to your events.

title: What Holds Tech Week's 1,500 Events Together
summary: A steady content feed lets attendees experience the parts they couldn't attend in person. For planners running multi-venue or community-driven events, it's a case for treating content as the infrastructure, not just the recap.

title: The CSR Activity That Started With a Handmade Birthday Card
summary: Jordan Lacey started Light the Candle at 17 to make birthday cards for foster children in her community. Now in the events industry, she is creating CSR activities that can be done anywhere.
